acceptance: DECISIONS A14: the nuclear station values are approved unchanged; natural-flow hydro uses the DUKES 6.3 2019-2024 mean load factor 0.3487 with the quarterly-derived monthly shape, accepted against DUKES 6.2 total hydro generation (2019-2024 mean 5.77 TWh, +-15 %). Plan 4.5 S8 nuclear target: within +-10 % of Energy Trends 5.1 (supplied basis).
applies_to: value-corrected profile only (corrections p05.firm-availability, p05.nuclear-generation-end-month and p05.hydro-dukes-load-factor; findings P5-09, P5-10, P6-10). The doctoral profile keeps the 35aadb3 constant availability 1.0.
compiled_from: docs/dev/REFERENCE_STATISTICS_FOR_AUTHOR_REVIEW.md sections 1 and 2 (second round with DESNZ xlsx, decision A11; reviewed by the author in A14)
calendar: fixed 365-day year of 48 half-hour periods per day starting 1 January 00:00 UTC; periods beyond 17520 wrap

nuclear.basis: Station load factor = PRIS 2019-2024 mean of station supplied energy / (PRIS reference power x hours) [D], applied as a constant derate of every period (no outage calendar in P0; planned-outage calendars are a P1 item). The model capacity is the EDF station capacity of value_uk_nuclear_policy_v1.json, so the energy-preserving model load factor is pris_load_factor x pris_reference_mw / model capacity.
nuclear.retirement: In the year of announced_generation_end 'YYYY-MM' (value_uk_nuclear_policy_v1.json, or generation_end_month_overrides below under p05.nuclear-generation-end-month), availability is zero from the first period of the following month (2030-03 -> period 4320). A station whose end has no month (Sizewell B '2055') runs the whole year; the asset is absent from model_unavailable_from_year.

heysham-2.source: reference statistics 1.6: N6 [V] (December 2024 extension of Heysham 2 and Torness to March 2030), N3 [V]; the policy file only says 2030

torness.source: reference statistics 1.6: N6 [V] (December 2024 extension of Heysham 2 and Torness to March 2030), N3 [V]; the policy file only says 2030

AGR.grade: [D] 2019-2024 mean of the four operating AGR stations

PWR.grade: [D] Sizewell B 2019-2024 mean; used for planned PWR/EPR projects (Hinkley Point C, Sizewell C)

national_aggregate.grade: [V2]/[E] DESNZ nuclear load factor 2023 72.4 %, 2024 72.3 % (N13, N15); consistent with DUKES 2026 table 5.10.B 2022-2024 mean 72.26 % [X]; used for an undifferentiated 'Nuclear' asset

nuclear.station_values_note: pris_load_factor equals the 2019-2024 arithmetic mean of reference statistics 1.4a (66.80 / 68.86 / 75.17 / 79.20 / 80.09 %) rounded to three decimals; A14 approved these values unchanged.

hydro_natural_flow.basis: Annual load factor x monthly shape (arithmetic mean 1 over the 12 months) applied to the dispatch capacity of run-of-river hydro.
hydro_natural_flow.load_factor_grade: [X] DUKES 2026 table 6.3, natural-flow hydro load factor, standard basis, 2019-2024 mean 34.87 % (yearly 36.05 / 41.59 / 32.77 / 30.60 / 33.82 / 34.41 %); chosen by the author in A14 (correction p05.hydro-dukes-load-factor)
hydro_natural_flow.monthly_shape_grade: [D] stepped shape from the Energy Trends 6.1 quarterly hydro load factors 2019-2024 (quarter factors 1.386 / 0.659 / 0.678 / 1.280), normalised to an arithmetic monthly mean of 1 (A14). On the 365-day calendar the period-weighted mean of this shape is 0.99883, so the modelled annual load factor is 0.3483.
hydro_natural_flow.capacity_note: GBP1 carries 2000 MW of natural-flow hydro: 0.3487 x 0.99883 x 2000 MW x 8760 h = 6.10 TWh, +5.8 % against the DUKES 6.2 2019-2024 mean of 5.77 TWh (A14 acceptance +-15 %) [D].

p05b_values.note: Values of P0-5b (p05.firm-availability without p05.hydro-dukes-load-factor), kept so a run recorded with them can be explained; superseded by A14.
